A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XtraGPT/ReviseQA research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V3 reports original model comparisons, human evaluations and a 54-paper before/after revision study, including Tables 3–8 and Figure 3.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds component ablations, AI-text detection analysis and a LoRA comparison in Tables 9, 10 and 14.

M1.justification: The inputs, criteria-guided curation, CPT objective and model family remain unchanged. V4's explicit HAC protocol and full-parameter training description clarify the existing procedure. LoRA is tested as an alternative, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ICLR 2024-derived ReviseQA, the six revision sections, paper-level evaluation and existing case studies. The added ablations and detector analyses reuse this coverage; they do not introduce another revision domain or task.

E2.justification: V4 adds a LoRA-tuned Qwen2.5-7B comparator in Table 14 and criteria/context-removal variants in Table 9. The existing general-LLM and backbone comparator sets remain unchanged, matching v3 Table 6 to v4 Table 5.

E3.justification: V4 adds component-removal controls, a LoRA experiment using one epoch and learning rate 2e-5, and two detector-based evaluation protocols over 7,000 test instances. Existing splits and primary evaluation settings remain unchanged. The reported curation total is corrected from 140,800 to 140,000 pairs, without establishing actual resampling.

E4.justification: V3 relies on backbone fine-tuning comparisons for implicit component validation. V4 directly tests criteria and document-context removal in Section 4.5, compares LoRA with full fine-tuning in Appendix H, and examines generated-text naturalness using two detectors in Appendix A. These substantially expand the supporting analyses.

E5.justification: V4 Table 10 newly reports standard deviations for Binoculars scores across source and revised texts. This adds descriptive dispersion reporting. The existing three-repeat paper-level t-tests, reported uncertainties and p-values remain unchanged; no increased run count or new seed information is stated.

E6.justification: V4 adds substantive component results: LC win rates against XtraGPT-7B are 44.65 without criteria, 34.71 without context and 42.17 for LoRA. Table 10 adds detector results, including AI probabilities of 38.22% and 37.27% for the 7B and 14B revisions. Existing benchmark, human-rating and paper-quality results are retained.

T1.justification: The problem mapping, conditional-likelihood objective, criterion-mixture argument and LC win-rate equations are mathematically unchanged. V4 adds no theorem, proof or substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: controllable collaborative revision, ReviseQA and XtraGPT, with superiority over same-scale baselines and near-proprietary quality. The revised title and fine-tuning wording clarify the existing focus rather than redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V4 explains why human-selected passages and single-round evaluation fit its collaboration protocol. It adds interpretations linking component ablations to coherence, full fine-tuning to long-context modeling, and detector scores to naturalness. Existing limitations concerning domain specificity, generator bias, iterative memory and judge reliability remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds explicit code, model-collection and revision-skill links, reports PaperDebugger integration, identifies training as full-parameter CPT, and supplies the LoRA epoch count and learning rate. The existing hardware and general hyperparameter table are retained; these disclosures do not establish changes to the original training procedure.

R1.justification: V4 adds references including LoRA, Fast-DetectGPT, Binoculars, PaperDebugger, EvoScientist and recent discussion works. Its positioning around author-controlled academic revision remains stable. Numerous other reference edits update publication metadata for already-cited works.

P1.justification: V4 edits the title, abstract and introductory language, expands the HAC explanation, moves Related Work from Section 2 to Section 5, and reorders the broader-impact and limitations discussion. Acknowledgments and cross-references are updated, while most existing exposition is retained.

P2.justification: V4 substantially reformats the title block, typography, text area and float placement. Workflow Figures 1–2 are revised, appendix prompts and criteria panels are redistributed and enlarged, and anchor labels and captions are clarified. Three new analysis tables are added.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens support for the central components through Table 9, clarifies human control and evaluation, and supplies resource links absent in v3. The gains are limited: LoRA uses one epoch while the general training table lists 10/20, and aggregate detector scores provide limited support for broad naturalness claims. Core results and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged, yielding a modest net improvement.
